fatal_errors: The proposed 500 °C annealing intervention is absent from the target, which investigates temperature-dependent nanoindentation and friction of the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu/Cu system.
The proposed oxide-layer and adhesion mechanism does not match the target mechanism involving dislocation density, HCP fraction, stacking faults, lattice disorder, and high-temperature softening.
The prediction of generally reduced friction conflicts with the target result that tangential force and friction coefficient increase and fluctuate strongly above 900 K.
The stated limits use unsupported macroscopic velocities and micrometer wear depths and confuse 900 °C with the target threshold near 900 K.
The evidence concerns CuMoTaWV films on stainless steel rather than FeNiCrCoCu on Cu; it does not validate 500 °C annealing for the target material.
The proposed ball-on-disc experiment does not specify an atomically resolved measurement capable of tracking dislocation lines, HCP atoms, stacking faults, or lattice disorder during wear.
explanation: The hypothesis is loosely aligned with the general aim of improving coating wear resistance and provides an unchanged-coating comparator, but it does not reconstruct the investigated intervention, nanoscale conditions, mechanism, threshold, or outcomes. Its evidence is an analogy from a compositionally and mechanically different film/substrate system; moreover, the quoted measured wear improvement is associated with a 300 °C-annealed CuMoTaWV film, while 500 °C is supported only as a processing condition. The operating ranges are asserted without evidence and are incompatible with the target simulation scales. A discriminating test would compare the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu/Cu model at 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K under identical indentation/sliding protocols while resolving HCP atom populations, dislocation-line length, lattice disorder, hardness, modulus, tangential force, and friction coefficient.
